title: Maximal multipoint Seshadri constants in positive characteristic
main_claim: For smooth projective X of dim n>=2 (n>=3 in the theorem, n=2 in a remark) over an algebraically closed field of char p>0, and L ample, there is r0 such that for all r>=r0 the Seshadri constant at the geometric generic r-tuple equals (L^n/r)^{1/n}.

issues.description: This is not a located gap. The argument is unusually strong. On P^2 with L=O(1), the same node, shear, unimodular and compression moves (the paper's constant w<l/100 is only a convenient sufficient choice) would give epsilon_10 = 1/sqrt(10), which is Nagata's conjecture for 10 points and still open. Every individual step checks, so the result deserves independent expert verification of the jet-transfer framework rather than signalling a known error.
issues.evidence: From Delta(1,1): d=3, W=3, c=1/3, T=9. Take t with a=2.829, b=0.171 and u=(1,1). The heights are b=0.171, -a=-2.829 and c=0.333, all distinct and with c>b. Their range is sqrt(10), so P_*=Delta(1/sqrt10, sqrt10). A brute-force search over these moves (depth 3, about 250k shapes) never beats the known epsilon_r(P^2) for r=2..8. It reproduces 1/2 and 2/5 exactly and stays below 3/8 and 6/17, so it is consistent with all known values.

coverage:
I read every section in full and checked each step line by line:
- Lemmas 2.2–2.6: least exponents and gradedness, the exposing weights in cases (i) and (ii), the formal transfer over k[[s]] (the F-point and jet-algebra isomorphism argument, and distinctness of the points), the unimodular step and coordinate compression.
- Prop. 3.1: the flag simplex bound via lexicographic division by the flag sections.
- Lemma 4.2, the node bound: Hensel roots in char 2, the branch parametrisations (xi=v(v+1)(2v+1), eta=0 near v=0, and symmetrically near v=-1), the weighted-degree bound 2i+3j<=W(i/A+j/B), and Q's area and convexity (b<c).
- The shear slice lengths.
- Lemma 4.3 constants: j>4, interval length jT/(1+T)>2, and i/d-jb=R-jW>=R/2.
- The final compressions and the area-to-maximal-slice computation.
- Lemma 5.1 (interior filling): the radius-rho ball estimate.
- Lemma 5.2: CRT interpolation, and E_m contained in N*lambda*P_*.
- Prop. 5.3: intercept bookkeeping (each carried intercept stays >= l, and 3w/l<1/16).
- Sec. 6: jets imply the curve bound via Hilbert–Samuel lengths, and the volume upper bound via the blow-up.
I also ran a numerical consistency search of the moves against the known small-r Seshadri constants of P^2.
sibling_notes: The sibling Higher-Dimensions paper (rank 332) also came back no_gap_found and made the same observation: the 2D reshaping would give Nagata on P^2 at r=10. This paper replaces the analytic limits with formal k[[s]] substitutions, and it uses the node y^2+xy-x^3 so that the two branches stay distinct in characteristic 2. Both changes check out.
